title: Integral strict-local sections agree with geometric-fibre sections
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, f:X→Y integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], s:Spec Omega→Y a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and (g',f',f,s) Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let F be a sheaf of Λ-modules on X_et [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let A be the strict henselization at s, ρ:Spec A→Y its structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], Z=X×_Y Spec A with projection p:Z→X. There exists a module isomorphism e:Γ(Z,p^*F)≅Γ(X',g'^*F), evaluated on the identity etale object on X'. For every small-model affine pointed neighbourhood j=(V_j,v_j), r_j followed by e.hom is R_(V_j,v_j). Here r_j is the actual unit and limit-leg restriction qcqsStrictLocalSectionRestriction [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-strict-local-module-comparison]; R is the unit for g' restricted along the lift with projections (f' followed by v_j,g') and the identity of X'. This theorem compares only sections on the two schemes and asserts no neighbourhood representative existence.

proof.text: Obtain the strict henselization local structure. Equip the geometric field with its residue-field algebra via descResidueField. The pointed-map theorem supplies the compatible ring map; construct t by Spec.map. Its pointed leg identity and the structural-map equation imply t followed by the structural map is s. Apply strictHenselizationStructuralMap_fiber_eq_closedPoint_compat from the canonical small-to-full comparison to this equation at the closed point; it puts the image of t at the closed point of the small model.

Construct i by pullback.lift from g′ and f′ followed by t. Its two projection equations follow by pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd. Pullback pasting yields the closed geometric fibre square. Integrality survives base change, and the integral strictly-henselian fibre restriction theorem makes the global-section map along i invertible.

Construct the required morphism r locally as the global inverse-image section map along i followed by the inverse-image composition comparison and terminal evaluation. Each factor is invertible, so take asIso r. For every small-model limit leg l apply unitSectionRestriction_comp. The graph of i followed by l agrees with geometricFibreSectionLift: the first projection follows from hi′, the first small-model projection identity and hpoint j; the second from hi and the second projection identity. Pullback hom-ext identifies the graphs. Expand unitSectionRestriction and cancel the terminal evaluation isomorphisms to get the required representative equation. This preserves the original small-model statement without the retired specialized definition or theorem.

Expand each former small-model qcqs restriction as unitSectionRestriction along the same small limit leg; expand the former comparison predicate as its germ equations. etaleSectionGraph is definitionally the former terminal graph. This changes only the spelling of the unit/restriction formulas and preserves every scheme, hypothesis, and conclusion.
